relevance_note: Table 3 gives individual-level data for two VEO-IBD patients with monogenic TNFAIP3 findings, e.g. '| P22/G1 | M | 48 | 72 | CD | Yes | TNFAIP3 |'.
method_note: Read the whole paper; Table 3 (patients as rows) transcribed by hand into a Python builder and every span checked by script against the Markdown. In scope: P22/G1 and P23/G1 (Gene column TNFAIP3, G1 = 'Monogenic findings') and the sibling of P23/G1 ('Sibling died from EBV-HLH'). The other 22 Table 3 patients (other genes) and the rest of the 36-child cohort are out of scope. Variant descriptions are only in Supplementary Table S2, which is not in this file, so both variant rows have variant_original_string 'not reported'. FH = Yes for both TNFAIP3 patients (first-degree relative with IBD) but no specific relative is described, so no row was created for that relative; it is not stated whether P23's sibling with EBV-HLH is the IBD relative. The Discussion's n = 2 group summary (recurrent bloody diarrhea, persistent fever, oral ulcers, arthritis, dermatitis, growth failure, autoimmune and immunodeficiency-like manifestations) was not used to assign features per person, as it gives no names; only 'both patients responded to Adalimumab' was used (treatment). 'Persistent fever' was recorded as a feature but not mapped to the checklist item 'recurrent fever'. Dermatitis was taken as a skin lesion. Group-level medians (CRP, ESR) were not attributed to individuals. Ethnicity 'Vietnamese' comes from the cohort-level description, not a per-person statement. is_proband left null for P22/G1 and P23/G1 (cohort paper, no proband wording). Ages: T1 and T2 cells are in months per the table legend; ISO values are given in months. Inconsistencies noted: the Table 3 legend defines 'HF: Family history of IBD' while the column header is 'FH'; the Methods call the study retrospective but the ethics statement mentions a prospective component; the two Data Availability statements differ (on request vs contained in article and supplement).
